parallel.requirements: Recognized both required front-end entry points, the lexer preprocessing/tokenization duties, the parser grammar/FIRST/FOLLOW/LL(1) duties, exact public functions, requirement files, and per-requirement git patch workflow.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used parallel delegation with a lexer worker and parser worker while the parent retained final integration, requirement-sized commits, local checks, and closure.
parallel.implementation: Implemented lexer preprocessing, token classification, error reporting, parser grammar loading, FIRST/FOLLOW computation, LL(1) table construction, and syntactic analysis; the parser still mishandled the aaa acceptance case.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Child work landed in the shared workspace; the parser child replaced Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp, then the parent edited the same file and delivered a clean git status with patch files and final summary.
parallel.verification: Compiled both programs and ran sample lexer/parser checks, including parser acceptance for aaabd and rejection for aaab; official evaluation later passed most checks but failed test_parser_accepts_aaa.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final parser deliverable remained wrong for the aaa grammar input despite broad implementation coverage and no harness timeout.

serial.requirements: Received the same prompt and requirement list, but the run did not progress far enough to demonstrate implementation coverage beyond initial task receipt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Ran as a serial control with actual_parallel_used false and protocol validation showing no spawn calls or child activity.
serial.implementation: The agent stream disconnected before meaningful editing, so the workspace retained little or none of the intended lexer/parser implementation work.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No parallel merge or shared-write lifecycle occurred; the attempt ended from process failure before a substantive final integration path.
serial.verification: Official evaluation completed afterward and showed only compile/some reject checks passing while most lexer and parser behavior tests failed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial trajectory is dominated by unknown_agent_error and stream disconnection, leaving the requested front-end implementation largely unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel read the prompt obligations for both LexicalAnalyzer/LexicalAnalysis.cpp and Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp and later claimed all 27 requirements were reviewed and implemented.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt but disconnected before acting on the requirement list or producing a substantive implementation plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel materially addressed the task requirements but missed one parser behavior; serial did not progress enough to cover the requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into lexer and parser inspectors while the parent kept final integration and commits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained a single-agent control with actual_parallel_used false and no child agent activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used concurrent ownership over task components; serial had no decomposition beyond the failed single process.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel component work converged through the shared workspace rather than an explicit stable file ownership contract for the parser entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not delegate, so it had no cross-agent interface or handoff contract to manage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main interface risk in parallel was shared ownership of Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp; serial avoided that risk by not using agents but also failed before progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel rewrote the lexer and parser implementation and then patched parser load-file behavior in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ended with a stream disconnect before meaningful source edits or implementation output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a nearly complete implementation with a parser edge-case bug; serial largely left original behavior unimplemented.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parser child completed a patch and the parent continued by modifying the same delivered file, so child output was joined through shared workspace side effects.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve because the serial process had no delegation and terminated early.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a real child-result lifecycle and post-child parent edits; serial had no result lifecycle beyond the failed process.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one shared workspace where the parser child replaced the parser entry point and the parent later patched the same file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no shared workspace writes across agents and protocol validation reports parallel_used false.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete parallel-only coordination error is a deliverable overwrite of Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp; serial had no comparable collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel compiled both programs and ran sample checks, then official evaluation passed most non-tail tests but failed parser acceptance for aaa.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial official evaluation passed only a small set of compile/reject checks and failed most lexer and parser behavior tests after the process error.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had meaningful but incomplete verification; serial had evaluator results over an incomplete process output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran to normal closure without official timeout, spent substantial runtime on implementation, and delivered a final summary claiming complete coverage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ended after an agent stream disconnect in roughly three to four seconds of agent runtime, with process_ok false.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was a completed but imperfect implementation; serial closure was a process failure rather than a completed engineering pass.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail because both current completed status evaluations set solution_passed to false. The runs nevertheless differ materially: parallel performed a broad implementation and failed only a parser acceptance edge case in the named results, while serial suffered an unknown_agent_error/stream disconnect before substantive task-solving and therefore failed most tests. The retained deliverable overwrite is a real parallel-side coordination defect, but it is not an outcome-differential explanation because serial did not pass and failed for a different process reason.
parallel_contributors: Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp was replaced by a parser child and then patched again by the parent, producing unstable final ownership of the required parser deliverable.
Parallel local verification covered sample parser strings but not the aaa acceptance case that failed in official evaluation.
serial_contributors: The serial process returned code 1 with process_ok false after a stream-disconnected task_complete event.
Serial protocol validation confirms no child or parallel work occurred, so its failure is a serial process interruption rather than a coordination collision.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel had a remaining ordinary parser correctness defect on test_parser_accepts_aaa.
Serial left most lexer and parser behavior unimplemented because the agent stream failed early.
evaluator_effects: The official pass/fail relation comes from status.json solution_passed fields; named test maps show quality differences but do not change the both_fail relation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process contributor but not a cause of a discordant official outcome.
